description.short: Robust, full-bodied mid-grown Ceylon black tea with rich maltiness — the cradle of Sri Lanka's commercial tea industry
description.overview: Kandy is the historic last royal capital of Sri Lanka and the hallowed ground where Ceylon's first commercial tea estate was established.
description.taste: Robust, satisfyingly rich, brisk without harshness, holding milk and sugar wonderfully
description.processing: Plucking → withering → orthodox rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: In 1867 at the Loolecondera estate in Kandy, Scotsman James Taylor planted 19 acres of tea, sparking the island's commercial tea trade.
history.development: Taylor's success turned Kandy into the epicenter from which tea cultivation spread across the central highlands.
history.modern: Today Kandy is classified as the premier 'mid-grown' region, yielding robust, satisfying teas that anchor world-famous breakfast blends.
interestingFacts: James Taylor's 1867 planting at Loolecondera in Kandy is the universally recognized birthplace of the Ceylon tea industry.
Kandy is a UNESCO World Heritage site home to the sacred Temple of the Tooth Relic, intertwining royal history with tea lore.
